documents.title: Local Author's Debut Novel Tops Bestseller List
documents.text: ASHBROOK (March 8) - Ashbrook resident Noor Haddad's debut novel, "The Salt Road," reached the top of the regional bestseller list this week, only a month after its release. [A] The story follows a family of traders crossing a desert in the 1800s and was inspired by letters the author discovered in an attic. [B] The book was first printed in a run of 3,000 copies, but its publisher, Larkspur Press, has since ordered a third printing of 20,000. [C] Haddad worked as a nurse for twenty years before writing full time and says that the early morning hours before work provided the only quiet time to write. [D] A book tour begins April 2 with a signing at Ashbrook Public Library.

documents.title: Delay in raw material delivery
documents.text:
To: Production Team
From: Wei Lin, Procurement
Date: March 20

Dear team,
I received word this morning from Orion Metals that our shipment of aluminum sheets, originally due on March 25, will arrive on April 3 because of a strike at the port of Hallsworth. This will affect the production of the Series 7 housings, which were scheduled to begin on March 26. I have contacted Delta Metals, our backup supplier, which can deliver 60 percent of the needed quantity by March 28 at a 12 percent higher price. I recommend that we accept this partial delivery so that we can begin production on schedule and complete the remainder when the Orion shipment arrives. Please let me know by noon tomorrow if you object. If we do not respond, Delta will offer the stock to another customer.
Wei Lin

choices: To cancel an order with a supplier
To request a price reduction from Orion
To report a delay and propose a solution
To announce a strike at the port
questions.explanation: Wei Lin reports the late shipment and recommends a partial backup delivery.

questions.prompt: What are the drawbacks of the Delta Metals option?

It lowers the quality of the housings
questions.explanation: Delta can deliver 60 percent of the quantity at a 12 percent higher price.

questions.prompt: What will happen if the team does not respond by noon tomorrow?
choices: The Delta Metals stock may be sold to another customer
Production will begin earlier than planned
The Orion shipment will be canceled
The price of the aluminum will drop
questions.explanation: Delta will offer the stock to another customer if there is no response.

documents.text:
Dear Customer Relations,

[A] The brochure promised an "ocean-view" suite, but my room overlooked the parking lot. [B] When I raised the issue at the front desk, I was told that no other rooms were available. [C] In addition, the spa, which was a major reason for booking this resort, was closed for maintenance for four of my seven nights, and no notice was given before my arrival. [D] I paid $2,450 for the package. I believe a partial refund is appropriate, and I am requesting $800. Please respond by September 15.
Sincerely,
Oliver Grant

documents.title: New e-mail and calendar system
documents.text:
TO: All employees
FROM: Aaron Kim, IT Director
DATE: March 1
SUBJECT: New e-mail and calendar system

On Saturday, March 16, the company will switch from the current e-mail system to Cloudmail. The transition will take place over the weekend and should be complete by Monday morning. During the switch, employees will not be able to send or receive e-mail from 6 p.m. on Friday, March 15, until noon on Sunday. All existing e-mails and calendar entries will be transferred automatically; however, attachments larger than 25 MB may need to be downloaded again. Training sessions (45 minutes) will be offered on March 6, 7, and 8 at 10 a.m. and 3 p.m.; sign up through the IT portal. Starting March 18, the old system will be accessible in read-only mode for 30 days. Questions can be sent to helpdesk@company.example.

To announce the hiring of new IT staff

documents.title: Brightfield Foods to Acquire Sunvale Snacks
documents.text: NEW HAVEN (May 6) - Brightfield Foods announced Monday that it will acquire Sunvale Snacks for $480 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by the end of the third quarter, will give Brightfield a leading position in the healthy-snack market and add 600 employees to its workforce of 4,000. Sunvale, founded in 2009 by two college friends, is known for its fruit bars and nut mixes. Brightfield CEO Dana Whitaker said Sunvale's brands will be kept, and no layoffs are planned for at least 18 months. The acquisition must still be approved by regulators and Sunvale shareholders. Shares of Sunvale rose 22 percent following the news.

documents.title: Update on the Brightfield announcement
documents.text:
To: All Sunvale employees
From: Greg Palmer, Sunvale CEO
Date: May 6

Dear colleagues,
As you have read in the news, Sunvale has agreed to be acquired by Brightfield Foods. I know this announcement raises many questions. Until the deal closes, we remain two separate companies, and our day-to-day operations will not change. Brightfield has guaranteed that existing positions will remain in place for at least 18 months, and benefits will be maintained. I will hold town-hall meetings on May 9 at 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. in the cafeteria, and a Q&A document will be posted on the intranet. Please direct media inquiries to our communications office.
Greg Palmer

Hartley Roofing
